content:
alice: Customer (k8s-saas) reports SSE chat_stream truncates after ~65s then client reconnects and immediately gets 401. They see partial final chunk and never receive the closing `data: [DONE]` event. Fronted by Cloudflare -> ALB -> nginx -> redwood origin. Customer repro attached.
support-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-2026 (auto) — https://support.redwood.ai/t/SUP-2026
ben: Can you paste the exact curl repro + response headers? Also which HTTP version are they using? ALB/nginx/Cloudflare all have different idle/buffering defaults.
alice: Repro (redacted):
```
curl -i -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=open-agg" 
```
Response snippets:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
transfer-encoding: chunked

data: {"id":"tok_...","chunk":"hello"}

data: {"chunk":"world"}
# connection stalls ~65s then client reconnects
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
content-type: application/json
{"error":"token_expired"}
```
Customer notes they run a Cloudflare Worker in front which does a simple fetch -> passthrough.
charlie: 2 quick things to check:
- ALB idle timeout default is 60s. For long SSE streams you want it >= expected idle gap or emit heartbeats. AWS console path: Load Balancers -> Attributes -> Idle timeout (secs).
- Cloudflare will buffer/respect origin headers depending on settings (Argo/Workers/Cache rules). With Workers, you need to ensure streaming passthrough (fetch(request) with keepalive). Cloudflare may still buffer for certain plans.
dana: On nginx proxy (if present) try these headers/config:
```
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection "";  # avoid "close"
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_cache off;
proxy_ignore_client_abort on;
# optional to tell some proxies not to buffer
add_header X-Accel-Buffering no;
```
Also ensure `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` is preserved by proxies.
ben: Envoy/ALB specifics:
- Envoy: check `stream_idle_timeout` and `connection_idle_timeout`. Set to 0s to disable idle kill or a high value (e.g., 300s) for long streams.
- ALB: increase idle timeout > 120s if you expect longer idle gaps.
charlie: The 401 on reconnect looks like a short-lived token issue. If client reconnects it may present an expired token. Two paths:
- Recommend clients refresh tokens before reconnect or retry auth on reconnect.
- Server can accept very short token grace window (not ideal), or provide a reconnect token that is valid for a few extra seconds.
alice: Customer tried adding a Worker-level heartbeat (they send `fetch()` with a small streaming transform that sends a `:\n` every 20s) — that seemed to keep Cloudflare and ALB happy for ~10 minutes but eventually the connection still drops and 401 appears on reconnect.
dana: We should also check origin ELB access logs + Cloudflare trace id for the exact timing of the close. Please ask customer to provide:
- Cloudflare cf-ray / trace id from request headers
- ALB access logs for the time window
- nginx access/error logs with request-id
- application runtime logs showing token validation on reconnect
charlie: Product-side mitigation: emit SSE comment heartbeats from our runtime every 15s: `:\n` (SSE comment) or a small keepalive event so middleboxes treat the connection as active. Example server-side pseudo:
```
while (stream_open) {
  if (no_output_for > 15s) write(":\n\n");
}
```
ben: Long-term infra fix: ensure ALB idle timeout bumped for streaming customers automatically (configurable per target group) and add a guide for Workers + Cloudflare settings (workers streaming body support + avoid response buffering). Also check token TTL/rotation flow to avoid immediate 401 after reconnect.
alice: Plan for customer: 1) Ask for cf-ray + ALB logs, 2) ask them to try client-side heartbeat or token refresh on reconnect, 3) we’ll push a temporary runtime heartbeat patch to eng-runtime to test for that customer. Escalating to eng-runtime oncall.
dana: Added task to eng-runtime oncall and pinned logs requirement. If you paste the cf-ray I will link to our Cloudflare account to check.
alice: Thanks everyone — looping in customer with steps. Will update ticket SUP-2026 when we have logs. :thumbsup:
